+# Glossary: Loa framework
+
+The shared language of the Loa agent framework, for humans and agents. It is mounted into every project with the framework and defines what each word means in day-to-day work; the mythic background of the names lives in the lore, and a project's own terms belong in that project's root glossary, never here.
+
+## Language
+
+**Beads**: The local-first task tracker that is the single source of truth for sprint tasks, decision tickets and their dependencies.
+_Aliases_: br
+
+**Bridgebuilder**: The automated pull-request reviewer that posts findings on a pull request and drives the iterative improvement loop of a bridge run.
+
+**Cheval**: The model-dispatch substrate through which every call to an external model provider is routed, with fallback, budget limits and cost accounting.
+
+**Circuit breaker**: The run-mode guard that halts a run after repeated identical findings, no progress, a cycle limit or a timeout, leaving the run for the operator to resume.
+
+**Construct**: An installable package of skills, personas and grimoire paths that extends the framework for a domain and may declare its own workflow gates.
+
+**DEC row**: One entry of the decision ledger, numbered DEC-NNNN, recording a decision, its alternatives, its status and the voice that proposed or decided it.
+_Avoid_: ADR, decision note
+
+**Decision ticket**: A question-type bead under a map epic whose resolution is a decision, not a build slice.
+_Avoid_: question task
+
+**decision:grilling**: The label of a decision ticket that talking can settle, answered in interview rounds with the operator.
+
+**decision:prototype**: The label of a decision ticket the operator needs to see before answering, settled by a spike and its verdict.
+
+**decision:research**: The label of a decision ticket that needs reading or sources, answered by a read-only research report and one confirming round.
+
+**decision:unblock**: The label of a decision ticket that a read-only probe settles by showing whether a suspected blocker is real; it never builds anything.
+
+**Dissent**: A second model's independent review of the same diff, triaged before a gate verdict.
+_Avoid_: second opinion, cross-check
+
+**Flatline**: The multi-model adversarial review of planning documents, in which independent voices review and cross-score each other before findings are integrated.
+_Aliases_: Flatline Protocol
+
+**Fog of war**: Decisions an effort can tell are coming but cannot yet phrase sharply; a map keeps them under Not yet specified.
+
+**Frontier**: The open, unblocked, unclaimed decision tickets of a map; in an interview, the questions whose prerequisites are already settled.
+
+**Golden path**: The five everyday commands (loa, plan, build, review and ship) that detect where the workflow stands and route to the right truename.
+
+**Grimoire**: The project's state area of planning documents, notes, reviews and records that agents read and write across sessions.
+
+**ICE**: Intrusion Countermeasures Electronics, the git safety layer of run mode that owns branch creation, push decisions and the refusal to touch protected branches.
+
+**Implement gate**: The hook that asks before an edit to application code made outside the implement or bug workflows.
+
+**Jack in**: To start an autonomous run under run mode; a run that has finished or been stopped for good has jacked out.
+_Aliases_: jack out
+
+**Kaironic**: Stopping at the right moment rather than after a fixed count: an iterative review loop ends when successive passes stop finding material issues.
+_Avoid_: converged
+
+**Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.
+
+**Known failure**: A recorded degradation with its symptom, the attempts made and a reading guide, consulted before triage so that prior dead ends are not retried.
+_Aliases_: KF
+
+**Lore**: The mythic and narrative background of the framework's names, kept apart from this glossary, which defines only working meanings.
+
+**Map epic**: The epic bead that parents an effort's decision tickets, paired with a map document of its destination, decisions so far, fog and exclusions; run mode never implements it.
+
+**Round**: One frontier of interview questions asked together and answered together.
+
+**Run mode**: Unattended execution of a sprint plan with a circuit breaker, wrapping implement, review and audit in a loop. Its states are running, halted and jacked out.
+_Aliases_: RUNNING, HALTED, JACKED_OUT
+
+**Seam**: A point where a test observes the system, declared in a sprint plan together with what it catches, what it misses and its prior art.
+
+**Spike**: A throwaway prototype on its own branch that answers one decision ticket; only its report and its verdict row reach the working branch.
+
+**Truename**: The underlying command that a golden-path command routes to, used directly by power users.
+
+**Verdict trailer**: The machine-readable last line of a review or audit feedback document, which must agree with its findings. Any critical or high finding forces a changes-required verdict.
+_Aliases_: LOA-VERDICT
+
+**Voice**: The party a decision or finding is attributed to: the operator, the agent, Flatline or dissent.
+
+**Zone**: One of the three permission regions of a repository: the System zone holds the framework and is never edited by hand, the State zone is read and written freely, and the App zone needs confirmation before a write.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# red-test-check.sh: verify a bug fix's red-before-green (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2).
+#
+# A /bug micro-sprint commits its failing test alone ("Red commit: <sha>" in reviewer.md) before
+# the fix. This check runs the test command at the red commit and at the green revision, each in
+# its own detached worktree under `mktemp -d`, and reports whether the test failed before and
+# passes after:
+#
+#   0 VERIFIED     red fails by assertion and green passes
+#   1 GREEN_FAILS  green fails (red failed by assertion)
+#   2              usage error, a commit that does not resolve, red not a strict ancestor of
+#                  green, a worktree that cannot be created, or a failing --setup
+#   3 DECOY        the test passes at the red commit
+#   4 NOT_A_RED    --test-file absent at the red commit, or the red run failed for a
+#                  non-assertion reason (collection, compile, import, command not found)
+#   5 TIMEOUT      a run exceeded --timeout
+# The red-side verdicts (5, 3, 4) are judged first, then the green side (5, 1).
+#
+# Honest scope (as validate-ac-verification.sh states for its own check): this proves the
+# command failed before and passes after. It does not prove the assertion is right, that the
+# test exercises the bug, or that the fix is the cause; the reviewer still reads the test. The
+# not-a-red patterns are heuristics over the red run's output: a test whose own assertion
+# output contains one of them reads as NOT_A_RED (a false negative the reviewer can overrule).
+#
+# What runs where: the test argv runs with cwd = each worktree, never through `bash -c`.
+# Uncommitted state in the live tree never counts and nothing is stashed. Present dependency
+# directories (node_modules .venv vendor target .tox) are symlinked from the live tree into a
+# worktree that lacks them (--no-link-deps turns this off); a test that writes into a linked
+# directory writes into the live tree's copy. --setup is split on whitespace into an argv (no
+# shell syntax; point it at a script for anything more) and runs in each worktree first.
+# The timeout uses `timeout`, else `gtimeout`, else a bash watcher (TERM, then KILL after 2 s,
+# to the run's process group); with `timeout`/`gtimeout` a test that itself exits 124 reads as
+# a timeout. One cleanup removes both worktrees (worktree remove --force, then prune) and the
+# scratch directory on every exit path, interrupts included.
+#
+# Usage: red-test-check.sh --red <commit> [--green <rev>] [--test-file <path>] [--setup <cmd>]
+#                          [--no-link-deps] [--timeout <s>] [--json] -- <test command...>
+# Run it from inside the repository's work tree. --json prints one object on stdout:
+#   {red, green, red_exit, green_exit, verdict, red_tail, green_tail, linked_deps}
+# (the exits are null when a run did not happen). Exit 2 errors print to stderr only.
+# =============================================================================
+export LC_ALL=C
+set -euo pipefail
+
+PROG="red-test-check"
+DEP_DIRS="node_modules .venv vendor target .tox"
+TAIL_LINES=80
+
+# Not-a-red output patterns (ERE, matched on the red run's output when it failed). One entry
+# per runner; extend here, never inline.
+NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS=(
+  # bats: the file did not load (gather failure), a parse error, a missing file or command
+  'not ok [0-9]+ bats-gather-tests'
+  'syntax error near unexpected token'
+  'syntax error: unexpected end of file'
+  'Test file .* does not exist'
+  'command not found'
+  ': not found$'
+  # pytest: collection and import errors
+  'ERROR collecting'
+  'ImportError while importing'
+  # node (node:test, jest, mocha): an unresolved import or a parse error
+  'Cannot find module'
+  'SyntaxError'
+  # cargo: the crate or its tests did not build
+  'could not compile'
+  # go (1.22 toolchain): build or setup failure of the test binary
+  'build failed'
+  '\[setup failed\]'
+)
+
+usage(){
+  echo "${PROG}: $*" >&2
+  echo "usage: red-test-check.sh --red <commit> [--green <rev>] [--test-file <path>] [--setup <cmd>] [--no-link-deps] [--timeout <s>] [--json] -- <test command...>" >&2
+  exit 2
+}
+die2(){ echo "${PROG}: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+strip(){ tr -d '\000-\010\013-\037\177'; }
+
+RED=""
+GREEN="HEAD"
+TEST_FILE=""
+SETUP=""
+LINK_DEPS=1
+TIMEOUT=600
+JSON=0
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --red) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--red needs a commit"; RED="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --green) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--green needs a revision"; GREEN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --test-file) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--test-file needs a path"; TEST_FILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --setup) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--setup needs a command"; SETUP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --no-link-deps) LINK_DEPS=0; shift ;;
+    --timeout) [[ "${2:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,4}$ ]] || usage "--timeout needs seconds (1-99999)"; TIMEOUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
+    --) shift; break ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '3,41p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) usage "unknown argument '$1' (the test command goes after --)" ;;
+  esac
+done
+[[ -n "$RED" ]] || usage "--red is required"
+[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || usage "a test command is required after --"
+case "$RED" in -*) usage "--red must be a commit, not an option" ;; esac
+case "$GREEN" in -*) usage "--green must be a revision, not an option" ;; esac
+case "$TEST_FILE" in
+  /*) usage "--test-file must be relative to the repository root" ;;
+  -*) usage "--test-file must be a path, not an option" ;;
+esac
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]] && ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then die2 "--json needs jq"; fi
+SETUP_ARGV=()
+if [[ -n "$SETUP" ]]; then
+  read -r -a SETUP_ARGV <<< "$SETUP"
+  [[ ${#SETUP_ARGV[@]} -gt 0 ]] || usage "--setup is empty"
+fi
+
+MAIN="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree"
+MAIN="$(cd "$MAIN" && pwd -P)"
+
+RED_SHA="$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${RED}^{commit}")" || die2 "--red '${RED}' does not resolve to a commit"
+GREEN_SHA="$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${GREEN}^{commit}")" || die2 "--green '${GREEN}' does not resolve to a commit"
+if [[ "$RED_SHA" == "$GREEN_SHA" ]] || ! git -C "$MAIN" merge-base --is-ancestor "$RED_SHA" "$GREEN_SHA"; then
+  die2 "red ${RED_SHA} is not a strict ancestor of green ${GREEN_SHA}: commit the failing test first, then the fix"
+fi
+
+RED_EXIT=""
+GREEN_EXIT=""
+RED_TAIL=""
+GREEN_TAIL=""
+LINKED=""
+
+# Report a verdict (text or JSON) and exit with its code.
+finish(){
+  local verdict="$1" code="$2"
+  if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+    jq -n --arg red "$RED_SHA" --arg green "$GREEN_SHA" --arg re "$RED_EXIT" --arg ge "$GREEN_EXIT" \
+      --arg verdict "$verdict" --arg rt "$RED_TAIL" --arg gt "$GREEN_TAIL" --arg linked "$LINKED" \
+      '{red: $red, green: $green,
+        red_exit: (if $re == "" then null else ($re | tonumber) end),
+        green_exit: (if $ge == "" then null else ($ge | tonumber) end),
+        verdict: $verdict, red_tail: $rt, green_tail: $gt,
+        linked_deps: ($linked | split(" ") | map(select(. != "")))}'
+    if [[ -n "$RED_TAIL" ]]; then
+      printf -- '--- red run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end red run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$RED_TAIL" >&2
+    fi
+  else
+    echo "${PROG}: red ${RED_SHA} exit ${RED_EXIT:-n/a}; green ${GREEN_SHA} exit ${GREEN_EXIT:-n/a}; linked deps: ${LINKED:-none}"
+    if [[ -n "$RED_EXIT" ]]; then
+      printf -- '--- red run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end red run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$RED_TAIL"
+    fi
+    if [[ -n "$GREEN_EXIT" && "$GREEN_EXIT" != "0" ]]; then
+      printf -- '--- green run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end green run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$GREEN_TAIL"
+    fi
+    echo "verdict: ${verdict}"
+  fi
+  exit "$code"
+}
+
+# D-7.6: the named test file must exist at the red commit.
+if [[ -n "$TEST_FILE" ]] && ! git -C "$MAIN" cat-file -e "${RED_SHA}:${TEST_FILE#./}" 2>/dev/null; then
+  echo "${PROG}: --test-file '${TEST_FILE}' does not exist at the red commit ${RED_SHA}: the failing test was not committed there" >&2
+  finish NOT_A_RED 4
+fi
+
+# WARN: a green that differs from red only in test files cannot be a fix.
+is_test_path(){
+  local p="$1" b
+  b="${p##*/}"
+  [[ -n "$TEST_FILE" && "$p" == "${TEST_FILE#./}" ]] && return 0
+  case "/$p" in */test/*|*/tests/*|*/spec/*|*/__tests__/*|*/testdata/*|*/fixtures/*) return 0 ;; esac
+  case "$b" in test_*|*_test.*|*.test.*|*.spec.*|*_spec.*|*.bats) return 0 ;; esac
+  return 1
+}
+nontest=0
+while IFS= read -r p; do
+  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
+  if ! is_test_path "$p"; then nontest=1; break; fi
+done < <(git -C "$MAIN" diff --name-only "$RED_SHA" "$GREEN_SHA" -- 2>/dev/null || true)
+if [[ "$nontest" -eq 0 ]]; then
+  echo "${PROG}: WARN: no non-test file changed between red ${RED_SHA} and green ${GREEN_SHA}; a pass there comes from test changes alone" >&2
+fi
+
+SCRATCH="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/red-test-check.XXXXXX")"
+SCRATCH="$(cd "$SCRATCH" && pwd -P)"
+WT_RED=""
+WT_GREEN=""
+RUN_PID=""
+WATCH_PID=""
+remove_wt(){
+  local wt="$1" d
+  [[ -n "$wt" ]] || return 0
+  # Unlink our dependency symlinks first, so nothing below can follow them into the live tree.
+  for d in $DEP_DIRS; do
+    if [[ -L "${wt}/${d}" ]]; then rm -f -- "${wt}/${d}"; fi
+  done
+  git -C "$MAIN" worktree remove --force "$wt" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+}
+cleanup(){
+  if [[ -n "$WATCH_PID" ]]; then kill "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
+  if [[ -n "$RUN_PID" ]]; then
+    kill -TERM -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+  fi
+  remove_wt "$WT_RED"
+  remove_wt "$WT_GREEN"
+  git -C "$MAIN" worktree prune >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  if [[ -n "$SCRATCH" && -d "$SCRATCH" ]]; then rm -rf -- "$SCRATCH"; fi
+  return 0
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+trap 'exit 130' INT
+trap 'exit 143' TERM
+
+add_wt(){
+  local path="$1" sha="$2"
+  # No hook from the shared hooks directory runs for our checkout.
+  if ! git -C "$MAIN" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null worktree add --detach "$path" "$sha" >/dev/null 2>"${SCRATCH}/wt-add.err"; then
+    strip < "${SCRATCH}/wt-add.err" >&2
+    die2 "could not create a worktree for ${sha}; nothing ran"
+  fi
+}
+
+link_deps(){
+  local wt="$1" d
+  [[ "$LINK_DEPS" -eq 1 ]] || return 0
+  for d in $DEP_DIRS; do
+    if [[ -e "${MAIN}/${d}" && ! -e "${wt}/${d}" && ! -L "${wt}/${d}" ]]; then
+      ln -s "${MAIN}/${d}" "${wt}/${d}"
+      case " $LINKED " in *" $d "*) ;; *) LINKED="${LINKED:+$LINKED }$d" ;; esac
+    fi
+  done
+}
+
+# Run argv with cwd $1, output to $2, bounded by TIMEOUT. Sets RUN_RC and RUN_TIMED_OUT.
+RUN_RC=0
+RUN_TIMED_OUT=0
+run_bounded(){
+  local cwd="$1" log="$2" flag="${SCRATCH}/timed-out" tbin="" start
+  shift 2
+  rm -f -- "$flag"
+  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then tbin=timeout
+  elif command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then tbin=gtimeout
+  fi
+  start=$SECONDS
+  # Job control gives the run its own process group, so a timeout or an interrupt stops the
+  # whole tree it spawned.
+  set -m
+  if [[ -n "$tbin" ]]; then
+    ( cd "$cwd" && unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_PREFIX && exec "$tbin" -k 2 "$TIMEOUT" "$@" ) > "$log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
+  else
+    ( cd "$cwd" && unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_PREFIX && exec "$@" ) > "$log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
+  fi
+  RUN_PID=$!
+  set +m
+  if [[ -z "$tbin" ]]; then
+    ( i=0
+      while kill -0 "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
+        if [[ "$i" -ge "$TIMEOUT" ]]; then
+          : > "$flag"
+          kill -TERM -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+          sleep 2
+          kill -KILL -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+          exit 0
+        fi
+        sleep 1
+        i=$((i + 1))
+      done ) < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1 &
+    WATCH_PID=$!
+  fi
+  set +e
+  wait "$RUN_PID"
+  RUN_RC=$?
+  set -e
+  RUN_PID=""
+  if [[ -n "$WATCH_PID" ]]; then
+    kill "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+    wait "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+    WATCH_PID=""
+  fi
+  RUN_TIMED_OUT=0
+  if [[ -n "$tbin" ]]; then
+    if [[ "$RUN_RC" -eq 124 ]] || { [[ "$RUN_RC" -eq 137 ]] && [[ $((SECONDS - start)) -ge "$TIMEOUT" ]]; }; then RUN_TIMED_OUT=1; fi
+  elif [[ -f "$flag" ]]; then
+    RUN_TIMED_OUT=1
+  fi
+  return 0
+}
+
+prepare(){
+  local wt="$1" name="$2"
+  link_deps "$wt"
+  if [[ ${#SETUP_ARGV[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
+    run_bounded "$wt" "${SCRATCH}/setup-${name}.log" "${SETUP_ARGV[@]}"
+    if [[ "$RUN_RC" -ne 0 || "$RUN_TIMED_OUT" -eq 1 ]]; then
+      tail -n "$TAIL_LINES" "${SCRATCH}/setup-${name}.log" | strip >&2
+      if [[ "$RUN_TIMED_OUT" -eq 1 ]]; then die2 "--setup timed out after ${TIMEOUT}s in the ${name} worktree"; fi
+      die2 "--setup exited ${RUN_RC} in the ${name} worktree"
+    fi
+  fi
+}

+# Glossary: Loa framework
+
+The shared language of the Loa agent framework, for humans and agents. It is mounted into every project with the framework and defines what each word means in day-to-day work; the mythic background of the names lives in the lore, and a project's own terms belong in that project's root glossary, never here.
+
+## Language
+
+**Beads**: The local-first task tracker that is the single source of truth for sprint tasks, decision tickets and their dependencies.
+_Aliases_: br
+
+**Bridgebuilder**: The automated pull-request reviewer that posts findings on a pull request and drives the iterative improvement loop of a bridge run.
+
+**Cheval**: The model-dispatch substrate through which every call to an external model provider is routed, with fallback, budget limits and cost accounting.
+
+**Circuit breaker**: The run-mode guard that halts a run after repeated identical findings, no progress, a cycle limit or a timeout, leaving the run for the operator to resume.
+
+**Construct**: An installable package of skills, personas and grimoire paths that extends the framework for a domain and may declare its own workflow gates.
+
+**DEC row**: One entry of the decision ledger, numbered DEC-NNNN, recording a decision, its alternatives, its status and the voice that proposed or decided it.
+_Avoid_: ADR, decision note
+
+**Decision ticket**: A question-type bead under a map epic whose resolution is a decision, not a build slice.
+_Avoid_: question task
+
+**decision:grilling**: The label of a decision ticket that talking can settle, answered in interview rounds with the operator.
+
+**decision:prototype**: The label of a decision ticket the operator needs to see before answering, settled by a spike and its verdict.
+
+**decision:research**: The label of a decision ticket that needs reading or sources, answered by a read-only research report and one confirming round.
+
+**decision:unblock**: The label of a decision ticket that a read-only probe settles by showing whether a suspected blocker is real; it never builds anything.
+
+**Dissent**: A second model's independent review of the same diff, triaged before a gate verdict.
+_Avoid_: second opinion, cross-check
+
+**Flatline**: The multi-model adversarial review of planning documents, in which independent voices review and cross-score each other before findings are integrated.
+_Aliases_: Flatline Protocol
+
+**Fog of war**: Decisions an effort can tell are coming but cannot yet phrase sharply; a map keeps them under Not yet specified.
+
+**Frontier**: The open, unblocked, unclaimed decision tickets of a map; in an interview, the questions whose prerequisites are already settled.
+
+**Golden path**: The five everyday commands (loa, plan, build, review and ship) that detect where the workflow stands and route to the right truename.
+
+**Grimoire**: The project's state area of planning documents, notes, reviews and records that agents read and write across sessions.
+
+**ICE**: Intrusion Countermeasures Electronics, the git safety layer of run mode that owns branch creation, push decisions and the refusal to touch protected branches.
+
+**Implement gate**: The hook that asks before an edit to application code made outside the implement or bug workflows.
+
+**Jack in**: To start an autonomous run under run mode; a run that has finished or been stopped for good has jacked out.
+_Aliases_: jack out
+
+**Kaironic**: Stopping at the right moment rather than after a fixed count: an iterative review loop ends when successive passes stop finding material issues.
+_Avoid_: converged
+
+**Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.
+
+**Known failure**: A recorded degradation with its symptom, the attempts made and a reading guide, consulted before triage so that prior dead ends are not retried.
+_Aliases_: KF
+
+**Lore**: The mythic and narrative background of the framework's names, kept apart from this glossary, which defines only working meanings.
+
+**Map epic**: The epic bead that parents an effort's decision tickets, paired with a map document of its destination, decisions so far, fog and exclusions; run mode never implements it.
+
+**Round**: One frontier of interview questions asked together and answered together.
+
+**Run mode**: Unattended execution of a sprint plan with a circuit breaker, wrapping implement, review and audit in a loop. Its states are running, halted and jacked out.
+_Aliases_: RUNNING, HALTED, JACKED_OUT
+
+**Seam**: A point where a test observes the system, declared in a sprint plan together with what it catches, what it misses and its prior art.
+
+**Spike**: A throwaway prototype on its own branch that answers one decision ticket; only its report and its verdict row reach the working branch.
+
+**Truename**: The underlying command that a golden-path command routes to, used directly by power users.
+
+**Verdict trailer**: The machine-readable last line of a review or audit feedback document, which must agree with its findings. Any critical or high finding forces a changes-required verdict.
+_Aliases_: LOA-VERDICT
+
+**Voice**: The party a decision or finding is attributed to: the operator, the agent, Flatline or dissent.
+
+**Zone**: One of the three permission regions of a repository: the System zone holds the framework and is never edited by hand, the State zone is read and written freely, and the App zone needs confirmation before a write.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# red-test-check.sh: verify a bug fix's red-before-green (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2).
+#
+# A /bug micro-sprint commits its failing test alone ("Red commit: <sha>" in reviewer.md) before
+# the fix. This check runs the test command at the red commit and at the green revision, each in
+# its own detached worktree under `mktemp -d`, and reports whether the test failed before and
+# passes after:
+#
+#   0 VERIFIED     red fails by assertion and green passes
+#   1 GREEN_FAILS  green fails (red failed by assertion)
+#   2              usage error, a commit that does not resolve, red not a strict ancestor of
+#                  green, a worktree that cannot be created, or a failing --setup
+#   3 DECOY        the test passes at the red commit
+#   4 NOT_A_RED    --test-file absent at the red commit, or the red run failed for a
+#                  non-assertion reason (collection, compile, import, command not found)
+#   5 TIMEOUT      a run exceeded --timeout
+# The red-side verdicts (5, 3, 4) are judged first, then the green side (5, 1).
+#
+# Honest scope (as validate-ac-verification.sh states for its own check): this proves the
+# command failed before and passes after. It does not prove the assertion is right, that the
+# test exercises the bug, or that the fix is the cause; the reviewer still reads the test. The
+# not-a-red patterns are heuristics over the red run's output: a test whose own assertion
+# output contains one of them reads as NOT_A_RED (a false negative the reviewer can overrule).
+#
+# What runs where: the test argv runs with cwd = each worktree, never through `bash -c`.
+# Uncommitted state in the live tree never counts and nothing is stashed. Present dependency
+# directories (node_modules .venv vendor target .tox) are symlinked from the live tree into a
+# worktree that lacks them (--no-link-deps turns this off); a test that writes into a linked
+# directory writes into the live tree's copy. --setup is split on whitespace into an argv (no
+# shell syntax; point it at a script for anything more) and runs in each worktree first.
+# The timeout uses `timeout`, else `gtimeout`, else a bash watcher (TERM, then KILL after 2 s,
+# to the run's process group); with `timeout`/`gtimeout` a test that itself exits 124 reads as
+# a timeout. One cleanup removes both worktrees (worktree remove --force, then prune) and the
+# scratch directory on every exit path, interrupts included.
+#
+# Usage: red-test-check.sh --red <commit> [--green <rev>] [--test-file <path>] [--setup <cmd>]
+#                          [--no-link-deps] [--timeout <s>] [--json] -- <test command...>
+# Run it from inside the repository's work tree. --json prints one object on stdout:
+#   {red, green, red_exit, green_exit, verdict, red_tail, green_tail, linked_deps}
+# (the exits are null when a run did not happen). Exit 2 errors print to stderr only.
+# =============================================================================
+export LC_ALL=C
+set -euo pipefail
+
+PROG="red-test-check"
+DEP_DIRS="node_modules .venv vendor target .tox"
+TAIL_LINES=80
+
+# Not-a-red output patterns (ERE, matched on the red run's output when it failed). One entry
+# per runner; extend here, never inline.
+NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS=(
+  # bats: the file did not load (gather failure), a parse error, a missing file or command
+  'not ok [0-9]+ bats-gather-tests'
+  'syntax error near unexpected token'
+  'syntax error: unexpected end of file'
+  'Test file .* does not exist'
+  'command not found'
+  ': not found$'
+  # pytest: collection and import errors
+  'ERROR collecting'
+  'ImportError while importing'
+  # node (node:test, jest, mocha): an unresolved import or a parse error
+  'Cannot find module'
+  'SyntaxError'
+  # cargo: the crate or its tests did not build
+  'could not compile'
+  # go (1.22 toolchain): build or setup failure of the test binary
+  'build failed'
+  '\[setup failed\]'
+)
+
+usage(){
+  echo "${PROG}: $*" >&2
+  echo "usage: red-test-check.sh --red <commit> [--green <rev>] [--test-file <path>] [--setup <cmd>] [--no-link-deps] [--timeout <s>] [--json] -- <test command...>" >&2
+  exit 2
+}
+die2(){ echo "${PROG}: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+strip(){ tr -d '\000-\010\013-\037\177'; }
+
+RED=""
+GREEN="HEAD"
+TEST_FILE=""
+SETUP=""
+LINK_DEPS=1
+TIMEOUT=600
+JSON=0
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --red) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--red needs a commit"; RED="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --green) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--green needs a revision"; GREEN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --test-file) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--test-file needs a path"; TEST_FILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --setup) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || usage "--setup needs a command"; SETUP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --no-link-deps) LINK_DEPS=0; shift ;;
+    --timeout) [[ "${2:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,4}$ ]] || usage "--timeout needs seconds (1-99999)"; TIMEOUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;

+    --) shift; break ;;

+[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || usage "a test command is required after --"

+case "$GREEN" in -*) usage "--green must be a revision, not an option" ;; esac
+case "$TEST_FILE" in
+  /*) usage "--test-file must be relative to the repository root" ;;
+  -*) usage "--test-file must be a path, not an option" ;;
+esac

+if [[ -n "$SETUP" ]]; then
+  read -r -a SETUP_ARGV <<< "$SETUP"
+  [[ ${#SETUP_ARGV[@]} -gt 0 ]] || usage "--setup is empty"
+fi
+
+MAIN="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree"
+MAIN="$(cd "$MAIN" && pwd -P)"
+
+RED_SHA="$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${RED}^{commit}")" || die2 "--red '${RED}' does not resolve to a commit"
+GREEN_SHA="$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${GREEN}^{commit}")" || die2 "--green '${GREEN}' does not resolve to a commit"
+if [[ "$RED_SHA" == "$GREEN_SHA" ]] || ! git -C "$MAIN" merge-base --is-ancestor "$RED_SHA" "$GREEN_SHA"; then
+  die2 "red ${RED_SHA} is not a strict ancestor of green ${GREEN_SHA}: commit the failing test first, then the fix"
+fi
+
+RED_EXIT=""
+GREEN_EXIT=""
+RED_TAIL=""
+GREEN_TAIL=""
+LINKED=""
+
+# Report a verdict (text or JSON) and exit with its code.
+finish(){
+  local verdict="$1" code="$2"
+  if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+    jq -n --arg red "$RED_SHA" --arg green "$GREEN_SHA" --arg re "$RED_EXIT" --arg ge "$GREEN_EXIT" \
+      --arg verdict "$verdict" --arg rt "$RED_TAIL" --arg gt "$GREEN_TAIL" --arg linked "$LINKED" \
+      '{red: $red, green: $green,
+        red_exit: (if $re == "" then null else ($re | tonumber) end),
+        green_exit: (if $ge == "" then null else ($ge | tonumber) end),
+        verdict: $verdict, red_tail: $rt, green_tail: $gt,
+        linked_deps: ($linked | split(" ") | map(select(. != "")))}'
+    if [[ -n "$RED_TAIL" ]]; then
+      printf -- '--- red run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end red run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$RED_TAIL" >&2
+    fi
+  else
+    echo "${PROG}: red ${RED_SHA} exit ${RED_EXIT:-n/a}; green ${GREEN_SHA} exit ${GREEN_EXIT:-n/a}; linked deps: ${LINKED:-none}"
+    if [[ -n "$RED_EXIT" ]]; then
+      printf -- '--- red run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end red run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$RED_TAIL"
+    fi
+    if [[ -n "$GREEN_EXIT" && "$GREEN_EXIT" != "0" ]]; then
+      printf -- '--- green run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end green run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$GREEN_TAIL"
+    fi
+    echo "verdict: ${verdict}"
+  fi
+  exit "$code"
+}
+
+# D-7.6: the named test file must exist at the red commit.
+if [[ -n "$TEST_FILE" ]] && ! git -C "$MAIN" cat-file -e "${RED_SHA}:${TEST_FILE#./}" 2>/dev/null; then
+  echo "${PROG}: --test-file '${TEST_FILE}' does not exist at the red commit ${RED_SHA}: the failing test was not committed there" >&2
+  finish NOT_A_RED 4
+fi
+
+# WARN: a green that differs from red only in test files cannot be a fix.
+is_test_path(){
+  local p="$1" b
+  b="${p##*/}"
+  [[ -n "$TEST_FILE" && "$p" == "${TEST_FILE#./}" ]] && return 0
+  case "/$p" in */test/*|*/tests/*|*/spec/*|*/__tests__/*|*/testdata/*|*/fixtures/*) return 0 ;; esac
+  case "$b" in test_*|*_test.*|*.test.*|*.spec.*|*_spec.*|*.bats) return 0 ;; esac
+  return 1
+}
+nontest=0
+while IFS= read -r p; do
+  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
+  if ! is_test_path "$p"; then nontest=1; break; fi
+done < <(git -C "$MAIN" diff --name-only "$RED_SHA" "$GREEN_SHA" -- 2>/dev/null || true)
+if [[ "$nontest" -eq 0 ]]; then
+  echo "${PROG}: WARN: no non-test file changed between red ${RED_SHA} and green ${GREEN_SHA}; a pass there comes from test changes alone" >&2
+fi
+
+SCRATCH="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/red-test-check.XXXXXX")"
+SCRATCH="$(cd "$SCRATCH" && pwd -P)"
+WT_RED=""
+WT_GREEN=""
+RUN_PID=""
+WATCH_PID=""
+remove_wt(){
+  local wt="$1" d
+  [[ -n "$wt" ]] || return 0

+name: Glossary Terms
+
+# cycle-128 FR-6 (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.2, D-6.3): every backticked framework
+# term in the kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) resolves to an entry or alias in
+# the framework glossary (.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md), or to an allowlisted code
+# identifier (.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt, at most 30 entries).
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh is the gate; the two control steps prove the
+# gate itself still bites. This check is Loa's own: it runs in this repository
+# only, never in a project that mounts the framework.
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+
+jobs:
+  glossary-terms:
+    name: Kernel terms resolve to the glossary
+    if: github.repository == '0xHoneyJar/loa'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
+        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5
+
+      - name: Check kernel terms against the glossary
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --report
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file GLOSSARY.md
+
+      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the miss fixture with exit 1)
+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          d=tests/fixtures/glossary/miss
+          rc=0
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --kernel "$d/kernel.md" --glossary "$d/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$d/allowlist.txt" || rc=$?
+          if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
+            echo "::error::check-glossary-terms.sh did not reject $d with exit 1 (got $rc)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "OK: miss fixture rejected"
+
+      - name: Negative control (the gate accepts the ok fixture)
+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          d=tests/fixtures/glossary/ok
+          if ! bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --kernel "$d/kernel.md" --glossary "$d/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$d/allowlist.txt"; then
+            echo "::error::check-glossary-terms.sh false-positive on $d"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "OK: ok fixture accepted"

+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

+}

+    run "$CHECK" --kernel "$FIX/miss/kernel.md" --glossary "$FIX/miss/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$FIX/miss/allowlist.txt"

+}

+    run "$CHECK" --kernel "$FIX/ok/kernel.md" --glossary "$FIX/ok/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$FIX/ok/allowlist.txt" --report
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/glossary-validator.bats
+#
+# validate-artifact.sh --type glossary (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.4, §4.5): an
+# H1, a context paragraph before '## Language', one-line '**Term**: definition'
+# entries of at most two sentences and 300 characters, _Avoid_: and _Aliases_:
+# only directly below an entry, no duplicate term or alias, WARN on a path or
+# file extension in '## Language'. Cases write temp files only.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
+    G="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/GLOSSARY.md"
+}
+
+# glossary <language-section lines...>: a valid head plus the given body
+glossary() {
+    { printf '# Glossary: test\n\nThe vocabulary of a test project.\n\n## Language\n\n'; printf '%s\n' "$@"; } > "$G"
+}
+
+val() { run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$G" "$@"; }
+
+@test "GV-1 the framework glossary validates with no warning" {
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-2 the root project glossary validates with no warning" {
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-3 both fixture glossaries validate" {
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/glossary/ok/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type glossary --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/glossary/miss/GLOSSARY.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "GV-4 a well-formed entry with _Avoid_ and _Aliases_ lines passes" {
+    glossary '**Dissent**: A second review. It is triaged.' '_Avoid_: second opinion' '_Aliases_: DIS, counter-review' '' '### Group' '' '**Voice**: Who decided.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "GV-5 a duplicate term fails, case-insensitively" {
+    glossary '**Spike**: A prototype.' '' '**spike**: Another one.'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'term "spike" duplicates term "Spike"'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-6 an alias that repeats a term or another alias fails" {
+    glossary '**Run mode**: Unattended runs.' '_Aliases_: RUNNING' '' '**Halt**: A stop.' '_Aliases_: running, run_mode'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'alias "running" duplicates alias "RUNNING"'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *'alias "run_mode" duplicates term "Run mode"'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-7 a definition over 300 characters fails" {
+    glossary "**Long**: $(printf 'a%.0s' $(seq 1 301))."
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'the definition of "Long" is 302 characters, over 300'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GV-8 a definition of exactly 300 characters passes; multibyte characters count once" {
+    glossary "**Edge**: $(printf 'a%.0s' $(seq 1 299))." "**Wide**: $(printf 'é%.0s' $(seq 1 299))."
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "GV-9 a three-sentence definition fails; two sentences pass" {
+    glossary '**Three**: One. Two! Three?'
+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'the definition of "Three" has 3 sentences; at most two'* ]]
+    glossary '**Two**: One sentence here. And a second (with a note).'

+}
+
+@test "GV-10 _Aliases_ without an entry fails" {

+    val

+}

+    val

+}
+
+@test "GV-12 a missing ## Language section fails" {

+    val
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# .claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2) against small
+# fixture repositories built per test. Every case also asserts that `git worktree list` in the
+# fixture shows only the main tree afterwards and that the live tree was not touched.
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh"
+    R="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/repo"
+    export TMPDIR="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/tmp"
+    mkdir -p "$R" "$TMPDIR"
+    export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
+    git -C "$R" init -q
+    git -C "$R" config user.email t@example.invalid
+    git -C "$R" config user.name t
+    git -C "$R" config commit.gpgsign false
+    # Base: a buggy add(); node_modules is ignored, as in a real project.
+    printf 'node_modules/\n.venv/\n' > "$R/.gitignore"
+    printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 - $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"
+    commit "base"
+}
+
+commit() { git -C "$R" add -A && git -C "$R" commit -q -m "$1"; git -C "$R" rev-parse HEAD; }
+
+# The red test: asserts add 2 3 = 5 and prints what it got.
+add_red_test() {
+    mkdir -p "$R/tests"
+    cat > "$R/tests/test_add.sh" <<'EOF'
+. ./lib.sh
+got="$(add 2 3)"
+if [ "$got" = 5 ]; then echo "PASS add"; exit 0; fi
+echo "FAIL: add 2 3: expected 5, got $got"
+exit 1
+EOF
+}
+fix_lib() { printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 + $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"; }
+
+# Status of the fixture after a run: only the main tree, no stash, the live tree as it was.
+assert_clean() {
+    local n
+    n="$(git -C "$R" worktree list | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
+    [ "$n" -eq 1 ] || { git -C "$R" worktree list; echo "worktrees left behind"; return 1; }
+    [ -z "$(git -C "$R" stash list)" ] || { echo "a stash was created"; return 1; }
+    [ -z "$(ls -A "$TMPDIR")" ] || { ls -la "$TMPDIR"; echo "scratch left behind"; return 1; }
+}
+
+rtc() { (cd "$R" && "$SCRIPT" "$@"); }
+
+@test "RTC-1 red fails by assertion, green passes: exit 0 VERIFIED with the red output printed" {
+    add_red_test; red="$(commit "test(bug): failing test")"
+    fix_lib; commit "fix(bug): add adds" >/dev/null
+    run rtc --red "$red" --test-file tests/test_add.sh -- sh tests/test_add.sh
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: VERIFIED"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"--- red run (last 80 lines) ---"*"FAIL: add 2 3: expected 5, got -1"*"--- end red run ---"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN: no non-test file changed"* ]]
+    assert_clean
+}
+
+@test "RTC-2 a decoy that passes at both commits exits 3 DECOY" {
+    mkdir -p "$R/tests"; printf 'echo "PASS always"\nexit 0\n' > "$R/tests/test_decoy.sh"
+    red="$(commit "test: decoy")"
+    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
+    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_decoy.sh
+    [ "$status" -eq 3 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: DECOY"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"PASS always"* ]]
+    assert_clean
+}
+
+@test "RTC-3 a --test-file absent at the red commit exits 4 NOT_A_RED before any worktree" {
+    printf 'x\n' > "$R/README"; red="$(commit "docs")"
+    add_red_test; fix_lib; commit "fix and test together" >/dev/null
+    run rtc --red "$red" --test-file tests/test_add.sh -- sh tests/test_add.sh
+    [ "$status" -eq 4 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"does not exist at the red commit"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: NOT_A_RED"* ]]
+    assert_clean

+    [[ "$output" == *"TIMEOUT"* ]]

+    assert_clean

+    local shim="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/shim" f b

+    for f in /usr/local/bin/* /usr/bin/* /bin/*; do

+        case "$b" in timeout|gtimeout) continue ;; esac

+    PATH="$shim" command -v timeout && { echo "the shim still exposes timeout"; return 1; }
+    mkdir -p "$R/tests"; printf 'sleep 30\n' > "$R/tests/test_slow.sh"
+    red="$(commit "test: slow")"
+    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
+    local start=$SECONDS
+    run env PATH="$shim" bash -c 'cd "$1" && shift && exec "$@"' _ "$R" "$SCRIPT" --red "$red" --timeout 1 -- sh tests/test_slow.sh
+    [ "$status" -eq 5 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: TIMEOUT"* ]]
+    [ $((SECONDS - start)) -lt 20 ]
+    assert_clean
+}

+    cat > "$R/tests/test_dep.sh" <<'EOF'

+. ./lib.sh

+    red="$(commit "test(bug): needs dep")"
+    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
+    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_dep.sh
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"linked deps: node_modules"* ]]
+    assert_clean
+    # the live tree's dependency survived the cleanup
+    [ -f "$R/node_modules/dep/index.sh" ]
+    run rtc --red "$red" --no-link-deps -- sh tests/test_dep.sh
+    [ "$status" -eq 4 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"Cannot find module"* ]]
+    assert_clean
+}
+
+@test "RTC-11 --setup runs in both worktrees before the test; a failing --setup exits 2" {
+    mkdir -p "$R/tests"
+    cat > "$R/tests/test_setup.sh" <<'EOF'

+    [[ "$output" == *"--setup exited 1"* ]]
+    assert_clean

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# .claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2) against small
+# fixture repositories built per test. Every case also asserts that `git worktree list` in the
+# fixture shows only the main tree afterwards and that the live tree was not touched.
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh"
+    R="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/repo"
+    export TMPDIR="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/tmp"
+    mkdir -p "$R" "$TMPDIR"
+    export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
+    git -C "$R" init -q
+    git -C "$R" config user.email t@example.invalid
+    git -C "$R" config user.name t
+    git -C "$R" config commit.gpgsign false
+    # Base: a buggy add(); node_modules is ignored, as in a real project.
+    printf 'node_modules/\n.venv/\n' > "$R/.gitignore"
+    printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 - $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"
+    commit "base"
+}
+
+commit() { git -C "$R" add -A && git -C "$R" commit -q -m "$1"; git -C "$R" rev-parse HEAD; }
+
+# The red test: asserts add 2 3 = 5 and prints what it got.
+add_red_test() {
+    mkdir -p "$R/tests"
+    cat > "$R/tests/test_add.sh" <<'EOF'
+. ./lib.sh
+got="$(add 2 3)"
+if [ "$got" = 5 ]; then echo "PASS add"; exit 0; fi
+echo "FAIL: add 2 3: expected 5, got $got"
+exit 1
+EOF
+}
+fix_lib() { printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 + $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"; }
+
+# Status of the fixture after a run: only the main tree, no stash, the live tree as it was.
+assert_clean() {
+    local n
+    n="$(git -C "$R" worktree list | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
+    [ "$n" -eq 1 ] || { git -C "$R" worktree list; echo "worktrees left behind"; return 1; }
+    [ -z "$(git -C "$R" stash list)" ] || { echo "a stash was created"; return 1; }
+    [ -z "$(ls -A "$TMPDIR")" ] || { ls -la "$TMPDIR"; echo "scratch left behind"; return 1; }
+}

+rtc() { (cd "$R" && "$SCRIPT" "$@"); }

+@test "RTC-1 red fails by assertion, green passes: exit 0 VERIFIED with the red output printed" {

+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# validate-artifact.sh --type sprint: the '### Seams Under Test' rule gated on the plan's

+
+# A plan with two sprint blocks; $1 = header date line (may be empty), $2 = seams in sprint 1
+# (yes|no|empty), $3 = seams in sprint 2 (yes|no|empty).
+seams_block() {
+    case "$1" in
+        yes) printf '### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|------|---------|--------|-----------|\n| `tool.sh` exit code | a wrong exit | prose | new |\n\n' ;;
+        empty) printf '### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|------|---------|--------|-----------|\n\n' ;;
+        *) ;;
+    esac
+}
+sprint_body() {
+    printf '### Sprint Goal\ng\n\n### Deliverables\n- [ ] d\n\n### Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] c\n\n'
+    printf '### Technical Tasks\n- [ ] Task %s → **[G-1]**\n\n' "$2"
+    seams_block "$1"
+    printf '### Dependencies\n- none\n\n### Security Considerations\n- none\n\n'
+    printf '### Risks & Mitigation\n| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| r | Low | Low | m |\n\n'
+    printf '### Success Metrics\n- m\n\n'
+}
+plan() {
+    printf '# Sprint Plan: x\n\n**Version:** 1.0\n'
+    [[ -n "$1" ]] && printf '**Date:** %s\n' "$1"
+    printf '**Author:** test\n\n---\n\n'
+    printf '## Sprint 1: Foundation\n\n'; sprint_body "$2" "1.1"
+    printf '## Sprint 2 (Final): Wrap-up\n\n'; sprint_body "$3" "2.E2E: End-to-End Goal Validation"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh: does every backticked framework term in the
+# kernel resolve to a glossary entry?
+#
+# The kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) is the only extraction scope. Every
+# backticked span outside fenced code is a candidate; a span is kept only when
+# it matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, which drops paths, scripts, flags,
+# commands and config keys (anything with "/", ".", "--", ":" or "(") as well
+# as spaced phrases and operators. A kept token resolves when it matches,
+# case-insensitively, a **Term** entry or an _Aliases_: token in the glossary's
+# "## Language" section, with a plural "s" or "es" folded and "-", "_" and a
+# space treated alike; or when the allowlist names it. The allowlist holds
+# code identifiers the heuristic cannot tell from a term: one token per line,
+# "#" starts a comment (give the reason there), at most 30 entries.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/check-glossary-terms.sh [--kernel PATH] [--glossary PATH]
+#                                 [--allowlist PATH] [--json] [--report]
+#
+#   --kernel PATH     default .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md
+#   --glossary PATH   default .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+#   --allowlist PATH  default .claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt
+#   --json            one JSON report on stdout
+#   --report          list every kept token with its resolution
+#                     (defined, alias, allowlisted or MISS)
+#
+# Exit codes: 0 every token resolves (a stale allowlist entry only WARNs)
+#             1 a token misses, or the allowlist has more than 30 entries
+#             2 usage, or an input file is unreadable
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+KERNEL="$ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+GLOSSARY="$ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+ALLOWLIST="$ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
+ALLOWLIST_MAX=30
+JSON=0
+REPORT=0
+ME="check-glossary-terms.sh"
+
+need_arg() { [[ $2 -ge 2 ]] || { echo "$ME: $1 needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }; }
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --kernel)    need_arg "$1" $#; KERNEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --glossary)  need_arg "$1" $#; GLOSSARY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --allowlist) need_arg "$1" $#; ALLOWLIST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --json)   JSON=1; shift ;;
+    --report) REPORT=1; shift ;;
+    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "$ME: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+for f in "$KERNEL" "$GLOSSARY" "$ALLOWLIST"; do
+  [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || { echo "$ME: cannot read $f" >&2; exit 2; }
+done
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$ME: --json needs jq" >&2; exit 2; }
+fi
+
+# Display names: repo-relative when the file sits under the repo root.
+rel() { case "$1" in "$ROOT"/*) printf '%s' "${1#"$ROOT"/}" ;; *) printf '%s' "$1" ;; esac; }
+DK="$(rel "$KERNEL")"; DG="$(rel "$GLOSSARY")"; DA="$(rel "$ALLOWLIST")"
+
+WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-glossary-terms.XXXXXX")"
+trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
+
+# 1. Kept kernel tokens, "line<TAB>token", first occurrence only, in order.
+awk '
+  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+  fence { next }
+  {
+    s = $0
+    while (match(s, /`[^`]+`/)) {
+      t = substr(s, RSTART + 1, RLENGTH - 2)
+      s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
+      if (t ~ /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ && !(t in seen)) { seen[t] = 1; printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, t }
+    }
+  }
+' "$KERNEL" > "$WORK/tokens.tsv"
+
+# 2. Glossary names, "kind<TAB>name<TAB>entry": kind is term or alias, entry is
+#    the **Term** the name belongs to. Only the "## Language" section counts.
+awk '
+  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+  fence { next }
+  /^## / { h = $0; sub(/^## +/, "", h); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", h); lang = (h == "Language"); next }
+  /^# / { lang = 0; next }
+  !lang { next }
+  /^\*\*[^*]+\*\*:/ {
+    t = $0; sub(/^\*\*/, "", t); sub(/\*\*:.*$/, "", t); gsub(/`/, "", t)
+    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", t)
+    entry = t; printf "term\t%s\t%s\n", t, entry; next
+  }
+  /^_Aliases_:/ {
+    a = $0; sub(/^_Aliases_:[[:space:]]*/, "", a); gsub(/`/, "", a)
+    n = split(a, parts, /,/)
+    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
+      p = parts[i]; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", p)
+      if (p != "") printf "alias\t%s\t%s\n", p, entry
+    }
+  }
+' "$GLOSSARY" > "$WORK/names.tsv"
+
+# 3. Allowlist entries, "line<TAB>token" (comment and blank lines dropped).
+awk '
+  { s = $0; sub(/#.*/, "", s); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", s)
+    if (s == "") next
+    split(s, f, /[[:space:]]+/); printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, f[1] }
+' "$ALLOWLIST" > "$WORK/allow.tsv"
+
+# 4. Resolve. "resolution<TAB>token<TAB>line<TAB>entry" for each kept token
+#    ("MISS" with an empty entry when nothing matches), then
+#    "STALE<TAB>token<TAB>allowlist-line<TAB>" for allowlist entries that no
+#    longer occur in the kernel and "REDUNDANT<TAB>…<TAB>entry" for ones the
+#    glossary already resolves.
+awk -F'\t' '
+  function norm(x) { x = tolower(x); gsub(/[-_ ]+/, " ", x); return x }
+  function put(map, k, v) { if (!(k in map)) map[k] = v }
+  # every spelling a name answers to: itself, its s and es plurals, and, for
+  # a plural name, its singular (the plural fold is applied here only)
+  function add(map, x, v) { x = norm(x); put(map, x, v); put(map, x "s", v); put(map, x "es", v)
+                            if (x ~ /es$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 2), v)
+                            if (x ~ /s$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 1), v) }
+  function lookup(map, x,   k) { k = norm(x); return (k in map) ? map[k] : "" }
+  FILENAME == ARGV[1] { if ($1 == "term") add(term, $2, $3); else add(alias, $2, $3); next }
+  FILENAME == ARGV[2] { allow[norm($2)] = $1; allowtok[norm($2)] = $2; next }
+  {
+    used[norm($2)] = 1
+    if ((e = lookup(term, $2)) != "") r = "defined"
+    else if ((e = lookup(alias, $2)) != "") r = "alias"
+    else if (norm($2) in allow) { r = "allowlisted"; e = "" }
+    else { r = "MISS"; e = "" }
+    printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", r, $2, $1, e
+  }
+  END {
+    for (k in allow) {
+      if (!(k in used)) printf "STALE\t%s\t%s\t\n", allowtok[k], allow[k]
+      else if ((e = lookup(term, allowtok[k])) != "" || (e = lookup(alias, allowtok[k])) != "")
+        printf "REDUNDANT\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", allowtok[k], allow[k], e
+    }
+  }
+' "$WORK/names.tsv" "$WORK/allow.tsv" "$WORK/tokens.tsv" > "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+
+kept="$(wc -l < "$WORK/tokens.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
+allow_count="$(wc -l < "$WORK/allow.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
+n_of() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k' "$WORK/resolved.tsv" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
+n_def="$(n_of defined)"; n_alias="$(n_of alias)"; n_allow="$(n_of allowlisted)"; n_miss="$(n_of MISS)"
+
+violations=()
+warnings=()
+while IFS=$'\t' read -r r tok ln entry; do
+  case "$r" in
+    MISS) violations+=("MISS: \`$tok\` ($DK:$ln) has no glossary entry; define **$tok** in $DG, add it to an entry's _Aliases_: line, or, if it is a code identifier, allowlist it in $DA with a '# reason' comment") ;;
+    STALE) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) no longer occurs in $DK; remove it") ;;
+    REDUNDANT) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) is already resolved by the glossary entry **$entry**; remove it") ;;
+  esac
+done < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+if [[ "$allow_count" -gt "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" ]]; then
+  violations+=("the allowlist $DA has $allow_count entries, over the limit of $ALLOWLIST_MAX; define the framework terms among them in the glossary instead")
+fi
+
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  jq -Rn --arg kernel "$DK" --arg glossary "$DG" --arg allowlist "$DA" \
+     --argjson allow_count "$allow_count" --argjson allow_max "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" \
+     --rawfile v <(printf '%s\n' ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}) \
+     --rawfile w <(printf '%s\n' ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}) '
+    [inputs | split("\t") | {resolution: .[0], token: .[1], line: (.[2] | tonumber), entry: .[3]}] as $rows
+    | ($rows | map(select(.resolution | IN("defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS")))) as $tokens
+    | {ok: null,
+       kernel: $kernel, glossary: $glossary, allowlist: $allowlist,
+       kept: ($tokens | length),
+       counts: {defined: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "defined")) | length),
+                alias: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "alias")) | length),
+                allowlisted: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "allowlisted")) | length),
+                missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS")) | length)},
+       allowlist_entries: $allow_count, allowlist_max: $allow_max,
+       tokens: ($tokens | map({token, line, resolution, entry: (if .entry == "" then null else .entry end)})),
+       missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS") | .token)),
+       stale_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "STALE") | .token)),
+       redundant_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "REDUNDANT") | .token)),
+       violations: ($v | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))),
+       warnings: ($w | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0)))}
+    | .ok = ((.violations | length) == 0)
+  ' < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+else
+  if [[ "$REPORT" -eq 1 ]]; then
+    awk -F'\t' '$1 != "STALE" && $1 != "REDUNDANT" {
+      printf "%-11s %-24s line %-4s %s\n", $1, $2, $3, ($4 == "" ? "" : "-> " $4) }' "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+  fi
+  for w in ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}; do echo "WARN: $w"; done
+  for v in ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}; do echo "$v" >&2; done
+  echo "kernel tokens kept: $kept; defined: $n_def; alias: $n_alias; allowlisted: $n_allow; missing: $n_miss; allowlist entries: $allow_count/$ALLOWLIST_MAX"
+  if [[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then echo "PASS"; else echo "FAIL" >&2; fi
+fi
+
+[[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
+exit 0

+@test "RTC-16 an interrupted run (TERM) still removes both worktrees" {
+    mkdir -p "$R/tests"; printf 'sleep 30\n' > "$R/tests/test_slow.sh"
+    red="$(commit "test: slow")"
+    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
+    (cd "$R" && exec "$SCRIPT" --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_slow.sh) > "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/int.out" 2>&1 &
+    local pid=$! i=0
+    while [ "$(git -C "$R" worktree list | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -lt 3 ] && [ "$i" -lt 100 ]; do sleep 0.1; i=$((i + 1)); done
+    [ "$(git -C "$R" worktree list | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -eq 3 ]
+    sleep 0.5
+    kill -TERM "$pid"
+    local rc=0; wait "$pid" || rc=$?
+    [ "$rc" -eq 143 ] || { cat "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/int.out"; echo "rc=$rc"; return 1; }
+    assert_clean
+}

+    grep -qF 'Red commit: <sha>' <<< "$t1"
+    awk '/^#### Task 2:/,/^### Acceptance Criteria/' "$m" | grep -qF 'The fix is a later commit and does not weaken the test'

+    grep -qF 'Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)' "$r"
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# validate-artifact.sh --type sprint: the '### Seams Under Test' rule gated on the plan's
+# header **Date:** (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.2; SEAMS_REQUIRED_FROM=2026-10-13).
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
+    T="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}"
+}
+
+# A plan with two sprint blocks; $1 = header date line (may be empty), $2 = seams in sprint 1
+# (yes|no|empty), $3 = seams in sprint 2 (yes|no|empty).
+seams_block() {
+    case "$1" in
+        yes) printf '### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|------|---------|--------|-----------|\n| `tool.sh` exit code | a wrong exit | prose | new |\n\n' ;;
+        empty) printf '### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|------|---------|--------|-----------|\n\n' ;;
+        *) ;;
+    esac
+}
+sprint_body() {
+    printf '### Sprint Goal\ng\n\n### Deliverables\n- [ ] d\n\n### Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] c\n\n'
+    printf '### Technical Tasks\n- [ ] Task %s → **[G-1]**\n\n' "$2"
+    seams_block "$1"
+    printf '### Dependencies\n- none\n\n### Security Considerations\n- none\n\n'
+    printf '### Risks & Mitigation\n| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| r | Low | Low | m |\n\n'
+    printf '### Success Metrics\n- m\n\n'
+}
+plan() {
+    printf '# Sprint Plan: x\n\n**Version:** 1.0\n'
+    [[ -n "$1" ]] && printf '**Date:** %s\n' "$1"
+    printf '**Author:** test\n\n---\n\n'
+    printf '## Sprint 1: Foundation\n\n'; sprint_body "$2" "1.1"
+    printf '## Sprint 2 (Final): Wrap-up\n\n'; sprint_body "$3" "2.E2E: End-to-End Goal Validation"
+    printf '## Appendix\n\n| Goal ID | Goal |\n|---|---|\n| G-1 | thing |\n'
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-1 a plan dated 2026-10-13 without the block fails and names each sprint missing it" {
+    plan 2026-10-13 yes no > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Sprint 2 (Final): Wrap-up (line"*"has no '### Seams Under Test' table"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" != *"Sprint 1: Foundation (line"*"Seams Under Test"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-2 the same plan with the block in every sprint passes without a seams WARN" {
+    plan 2026-10-13 yes yes > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" != *"Seams Under Test"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-3 a later date also requires it; a heading with no table row counts as missing" {
+    plan 2026-11-02 empty yes > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Sprint 1: Foundation (line"*"has no '### Seams Under Test' table with at least one row"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-4 a plan dated 2026-10-12 without the block passes with one WARN" {
+    plan 2026-10-12 no no > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: 2026-10-12 plan: 2 sprint block(s) without a '### Seams Under Test' table"* ]]
+    [ "$(grep -c 'Seams Under Test' <<< "$output")" -eq 1 ]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-5 an undated plan passes with one WARN" {
+    plan "" no no > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: undated plan: 2 sprint block(s)"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-6 a Date line below the first H2 is not the header date (the plan reads as undated)" {
+    { plan "" no no; printf '\n## Notes\n\n**Date:** 2026-12-01\n'; } > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: undated plan"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-7 a Seams heading inside fenced code does not count; a block under a later H2 does not either" {
+    {
+        plan 2026-10-13 yes no | sed '/^## Appendix/,$d'
+        printf '```\n### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| a | b | c | d |\n```\n\n'
+        printf '## Risk Register\n\n### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| a | b | c | d |\n\n'
+        printf '## Appendix\n\n| Goal ID | Goal |\n|---|---|\n| G-1 | thing |\n'
+    } > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"Sprint 2 (Final): Wrap-up (line"*"Seams Under Test"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-8 this cycle's grimoires/loa/sprint.md passes" {
+    [ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/sprint.md" ] || skip "no live sprint plan in this checkout"
+    grep -q '^\*\*Date:\*\* 2026-10-1[3-9]' "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/sprint.md" || skip "the live plan is not the cycle-128 plan"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" != *"Seams Under Test"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-9 the archived cycle-127 plan (dated 2026-10-07) gains only a WARN from the rule" {
+    local f="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/sprint-seams/cycle-127-sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$f"
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: 2026-10-07 plan: 1 sprint block(s) without a '### Seams Under Test' table"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" != *"has no '### Seams Under Test' table with"* ]]
+    # The plan predates the template's Risks & Mitigation / Success Metrics sections and fails
+    # on those alone, exactly as it did before the seams rule; the rule adds no violation.
+    local others
+    others="$(grep -v '^WARN\|^INFO' <<< "$output" | grep -vc "missing required section '### \(Risks & Mitigation\|Success Metrics\)'" || true)"
+    [ "$others" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "SEAMS-10 the shipped sprint template carries the block in each full sprint block" {
+    local t="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/planning-sprints/resources/templates/sprint-template.md"
+    [ "$(grep -c '^### Seams Under Test$' "$t")" -eq 2 ]
+    [ "$(grep -c '^| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |$' "$t")" -eq 2 ]
+}

+# The kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) is the only extraction scope. Every
+# backticked span outside fenced code is a candidate; a span is kept only when
+# it matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, which drops paths, scripts, flags,
+# commands and config keys (anything with "/", ".", "--", ":" or "(") as well
+# as spaced phrases and operators. A kept token resolves when it matches,
+# case-insensitively, a **Term** entry or an _Aliases_: token in the glossary's
+# "## Language" section, with a plural "s" or "es" folded and "-", "_" and a
+# space treated alike; or when the allowlist names it. The allowlist holds
+# code identifiers the heuristic cannot tell from a term: one token per line,
+# "#" starts a comment (give the reason there), at most 30 entries.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/check-glossary-terms.sh [--kernel PATH] [--glossary PATH]
+#                                 [--allowlist PATH] [--json] [--report]
+#
+#   --kernel PATH     default .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md
+#   --glossary PATH   default .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+#   --allowlist PATH  default .claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt
+#   --json            one JSON report on stdout
+#   --report          list every kept token with its resolution
+#                     (defined, alias, allowlisted or MISS)
+#
+# Exit codes: 0 every token resolves (a stale allowlist entry only WARNs)
+#             1 a token misses, or the allowlist has more than 30 entries
+#             2 usage, or an input file is unreadable
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+KERNEL="$ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+GLOSSARY="$ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+ALLOWLIST="$ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
+ALLOWLIST_MAX=30
+JSON=0
+REPORT=0
+ME="check-glossary-terms.sh"
+
+need_arg() { [[ $2 -ge 2 ]] || { echo "$ME: $1 needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }; }
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --kernel)    need_arg "$1" $#; KERNEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --glossary)  need_arg "$1" $#; GLOSSARY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --allowlist) need_arg "$1" $#; ALLOWLIST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --json)   JSON=1; shift ;;
+    --report) REPORT=1; shift ;;
+    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "$ME: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+for f in "$KERNEL" "$GLOSSARY" "$ALLOWLIST"; do
+  [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || { echo "$ME: cannot read $f" >&2; exit 2; }
+done
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$ME: --json needs jq" >&2; exit 2; }
+fi
+
+# Display names: repo-relative when the file sits under the repo root.
+rel() { case "$1" in "$ROOT"/*) printf '%s' "${1#"$ROOT"/}" ;; *) printf '%s' "$1" ;; esac; }
+DK="$(rel "$KERNEL")"; DG="$(rel "$GLOSSARY")"; DA="$(rel "$ALLOWLIST")"
+
+WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-glossary-terms.XXXXXX")"
+trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
+
+# 1. Kept kernel tokens, "line<TAB>token", first occurrence only, in order.
+awk '
+  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+  fence { next }
+  {
+    s = $0
+    while (match(s, /`[^`]+`/)) {
+      t = substr(s, RSTART + 1, RLENGTH - 2)
+      s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
+      if (t ~ /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ && !(t in seen)) { seen[t] = 1; printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, t }
+    }
+  }
+' "$KERNEL" > "$WORK/tokens.tsv"
+
+# 2. Glossary names, "kind<TAB>name<TAB>entry": kind is term or alias, entry is
+#    the **Term** the name belongs to. Only the "## Language" section counts.
+awk '
+  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+  fence { next }
+  /^## / { h = $0; sub(/^## +/, "", h); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", h); lang = (h == "Language"); next }
+  /^# / { lang = 0; next }
+  !lang { next }
+  /^\*\*[^*]+\*\*:/ {
+    t = $0; sub(/^\*\*/, "", t); sub(/\*\*:.*$/, "", t); gsub(/`/, "", t)
+    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", t)
+    entry = t; printf "term\t%s\t%s\n", t, entry; next
+  }
+  /^_Aliases_:/ {
+    a = $0; sub(/^_Aliases_:[[:space:]]*/, "", a); gsub(/`/, "", a)
+    n = split(a, parts, /,/)
+    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
+      p = parts[i]; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", p)
+      if (p != "") printf "alias\t%s\t%s\n", p, entry
+    }
+  }
+' "$GLOSSARY" > "$WORK/names.tsv"
+
+# 3. Allowlist entries, "line<TAB>token" (comment and blank lines dropped).
+awk '
+  { s = $0; sub(/#.*/, "", s); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", s)
+    if (s == "") next
+    split(s, f, /[[:space:]]+/); printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, f[1] }
+' "$ALLOWLIST" > "$WORK/allow.tsv"
+
+# 4. Resolve. "resolution<TAB>token<TAB>line<TAB>entry" for each kept token
+#    ("MISS" with an empty entry when nothing matches), then
+#    "STALE<TAB>token<TAB>allowlist-line<TAB>" for allowlist entries that no
+#    longer occur in the kernel and "REDUNDANT<TAB>…<TAB>entry" for ones the
+#    glossary already resolves.
+awk -F'\t' '
+  function norm(x) { x = tolower(x); gsub(/[-_ ]+/, " ", x); return x }
+  function put(map, k, v) { if (!(k in map)) map[k] = v }
+  # every spelling a name answers to: itself, its s and es plurals, and, for
+  # a plural name, its singular (the plural fold is applied here only)
+  function add(map, x, v) { x = norm(x); put(map, x, v); put(map, x "s", v); put(map, x "es", v)
+                            if (x ~ /es$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 2), v)
+                            if (x ~ /s$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 1), v) }
+  function lookup(map, x,   k) { k = norm(x); return (k in map) ? map[k] : "" }
+  FILENAME == ARGV[1] { if ($1 == "term") add(term, $2, $3); else add(alias, $2, $3); next }
+  FILENAME == ARGV[2] { allow[norm($2)] = $1; allowtok[norm($2)] = $2; next }
+  {
+    used[norm($2)] = 1
+    if ((e = lookup(term, $2)) != "") r = "defined"
+    else if ((e = lookup(alias, $2)) != "") r = "alias"
+    else if (norm($2) in allow) { r = "allowlisted"; e = "" }
+    else { r = "MISS"; e = "" }
+    printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", r, $2, $1, e
+  }
+  END {
+    for (k in allow) {
+      if (!(k in used)) printf "STALE\t%s\t%s\t\n", allowtok[k], allow[k]
+      else if ((e = lookup(term, allowtok[k])) != "" || (e = lookup(alias, allowtok[k])) != "")
+        printf "REDUNDANT\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", allowtok[k], allow[k], e
+    }
+  }
+' "$WORK/names.tsv" "$WORK/allow.tsv" "$WORK/tokens.tsv" > "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+
+kept="$(wc -l < "$WORK/tokens.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
+allow_count="$(wc -l < "$WORK/allow.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
+n_of() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k' "$WORK/resolved.tsv" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
+n_def="$(n_of defined)"; n_alias="$(n_of alias)"; n_allow="$(n_of allowlisted)"; n_miss="$(n_of MISS)"
+
+violations=()
+warnings=()
+while IFS=$'\t' read -r r tok ln entry; do
+  case "$r" in
+    MISS) violations+=("MISS: \`$tok\` ($DK:$ln) has no glossary entry; define **$tok** in $DG, add it to an entry's _Aliases_: line, or, if it is a code identifier, allowlist it in $DA with a '# reason' comment") ;;
+    STALE) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) no longer occurs in $DK; remove it") ;;
+    REDUNDANT) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) is already resolved by the glossary entry **$entry**; remove it") ;;
+  esac
+done < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+if [[ "$allow_count" -gt "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" ]]; then
+  violations+=("the allowlist $DA has $allow_count entries, over the limit of $ALLOWLIST_MAX; define the framework terms among them in the glossary instead")
+fi
+
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  jq -Rn --arg kernel "$DK" --arg glossary "$DG" --arg allowlist "$DA" \
+     --argjson allow_count "$allow_count" --argjson allow_max "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" \
+     --rawfile v <(printf '%s\n' ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}) \
+     --rawfile w <(printf '%s\n' ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}) '
+    [inputs | split("\t") | {resolution: .[0], token: .[1], line: (.[2] | tonumber), entry: .[3]}] as $rows
+    | ($rows | map(select(.resolution | IN("defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS")))) as $tokens
+    | {ok: null,
+       kernel: $kernel, glossary: $glossary, allowlist: $allowlist,
+       kept: ($tokens | length),
+       counts: {defined: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "defined")) | length),
+                alias: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "alias")) | length),
+                allowlisted: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "allowlisted")) | length),
+                missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS")) | length)},
+       allowlist_entries: $allow_count, allowlist_max: $allow_max,
+       tokens: ($tokens | map({token, line, resolution, entry: (if .entry == "" then null else .entry end)})),
+       missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS") | .token)),
+       stale_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "STALE") | .token)),
+       redundant_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "REDUNDANT") | .token)),
+       violations: ($v | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))),
+       warnings: ($w | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0)))}
+    | .ok = ((.violations | length) == 0)
+  ' < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+else
+  if [[ "$REPORT" -eq 1 ]]; then
+    awk -F'\t' '$1 != "STALE" && $1 != "REDUNDANT" {
+      printf "%-11s %-24s line %-4s %s\n", $1, $2, $3, ($4 == "" ? "" : "-> " $4) }' "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+  fi
+  for w in ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}; do echo "WARN: $w"; done
+  for v in ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}; do echo "$v" >&2; done
+  echo "kernel tokens kept: $kept; defined: $n_def; alias: $n_alias; allowlisted: $n_allow; missing: $n_miss; allowlist entries: $allow_count/$ALLOWLIST_MAX"
+  if [[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then echo "PASS"; else echo "FAIL" >&2; fi
+fi
+
+[[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
+exit 0

+name: Glossary Terms
+
+# cycle-128 FR-6 (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.2, D-6.3): every backticked framework
+# term in the kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) resolves to an entry or alias in
+# the framework glossary (.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md), or to an allowlisted code
+# identifier (.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt, at most 30 entries).
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh is the gate; the two control steps prove the
+# gate itself still bites. This check is Loa's own: it runs in this repository
+# only, never in a project that mounts the framework.
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+
+jobs:
+  glossary-terms:
+    name: Kernel terms resolve to the glossary
+    if: github.repository == '0xHoneyJar/loa'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
+        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5
+
+      - name: Check kernel terms against the glossary
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --report
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file GLOSSARY.md
+
+      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the miss fixture with exit 1)
+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          d=tests/fixtures/glossary/miss
+          rc=0
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --kernel "$d/kernel.md" --glossary "$d/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$d/allowlist.txt" || rc=$?
+          if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
+            echo "::error::check-glossary-terms.sh did not reject $d with exit 1 (got $rc)"

+          fi
+          echo "OK: miss fixture rejected"
+
+      - name: Negative control (the gate accepts the ok fixture)
+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure

+            exit 1
+          fi

+

+name: Glossary Terms
+
+# cycle-128 FR-6 (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.2, D-6.3): every backticked framework

+# identifier (.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt, at most 30 entries).
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh is the gate; the two control steps prove the
+# gate itself still bites. This check is Loa's own: it runs in this repository
+# only, never in a project that mounts the framework.
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+
+jobs:
+  glossary-terms:
+    name: Kernel terms resolve to the glossary
+    if: github.repository == '0xHoneyJar/loa'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
+        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5
+
+      - name: Check kernel terms against the glossary
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --report
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file GLOSSARY.md
+
+      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the miss fixture with exit 1)
+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          d=tests/fixtures/glossary/miss
+          rc=0
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --kernel "$d/kernel.md" --glossary "$d/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$d/allowlist.txt" || rc=$?

+            echo "::error::check-glossary-terms.sh did not reject $d with exit 1 (got $rc)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "OK: miss fixture rejected"

+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure

+            echo "::error::check-glossary-terms.sh false-positive on $d"
