+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/glossary-terms.bats
+#
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.2, §5.3) keeps every
+# backticked span of the kernel that matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$ outside
+# fenced code and fails unless each one resolves to a glossary **Term**, an
+# _Aliases_: token (case-insensitive, plural s/es folded) or an allowlist line
+# (at most 30). Every case below works on temp copies; the live kernel,
+# glossary and allowlist are only ever read.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh"
+    KERNEL="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    GLOSSARY="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+    ALLOW="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
+    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/glossary"
+    W="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    printf '# Glossary: t\nTest vocabulary.\n\n## Language\n\n**Widget**: A thing.\n\n**Run mode**: Unattended runs.\n_Aliases_: RUNNING, JACKED_OUT\n\n**Box**: A container.\n' > "$W/g.md"
+    printf '# test allowlist\nparse_it   # code identifier\n' > "$W/a.txt"
+}
+
+# check <kernel text>: run the checker on a temp kernel with the temp glossary and allowlist
+check() {
+    printf '%s\n' "$1" > "$W/k.md"
+    shift
+    run "$CHECK" --kernel "$W/k.md" --glossary "$W/g.md" --allowlist "$W/a.txt" "$@"
+}
+
+@test "GT-1 the live kernel, framework glossary and allowlist pass" {
+    run "$CHECK"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"missing: 0"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"PASS"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-2 removing a term from a copy of the glossary fails and names the token" {
+    grep -v '^_Aliases_: br$' "$GLOSSARY" > "$W/glossary.md"
+    run "$CHECK" --glossary "$W/glossary.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `br`'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"define **br**"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"_Aliases_: line"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"allowlist it in"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-3 removing the run mode entry from a copy fails on each of its aliases" {
+    awk '/^\*\*Run mode\*\*:/ { skip = 1; next } skip && /^_Aliases_:/ { skip = 0; next } { skip = 0; print }' "$GLOSSARY" > "$W/glossary.md"
+    run "$CHECK" --glossary "$W/glossary.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `RUNNING`'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `HALTED`'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `JACKED_OUT`'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-4 matching is case-insensitive and folds s and es plurals" {
+    check 'Use a `widget`, two `Widgets`, `boxes` and `BOX`.' --report
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     widget"*"-> Widget"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     Widgets"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     boxes"*"-> Box"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     BOX"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-4b a singular token resolves to a plural term" {
+    printf '# Glossary: t\nctx\n\n## Language\n\n**Beads**: A tracker.\n\n**Matches**: Pairs.\n' > "$W/g.md"
+    check 'One `bead`, one `match`, many `BEADS`.' --report
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     bead "*"-> Beads"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     match "*"-> Matches"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-5 an _Aliases_: token resolves to its entry; a multi-word term matches with - or _" {
+    check 'States: `running`, `JACKED_OUT`; also `run-mode` and `run_mode`.' --report
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"alias       running"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"alias       JACKED_OUT"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     run-mode"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     run_mode"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-6 an undefined token fails; a token close to a term does not resolve by accident" {
+    check 'A `Widgetry` and a `Sprocket`.'
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `Widgetry`'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `Sprocket`'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"missing: 2"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-7 tokens inside fenced code are ignored (backtick and tilde fences)" {
+    check $'Prose `Widget`.\n```bash\necho `Sprocket`\n```\n~~~\n`Gizmo`\n~~~\n  ```\n  `Indented`\n  ```'
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"kernel tokens kept: 1;"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-8 the shape heuristic drops paths, files, flags, keys, calls, commands, phrases and operators" {
+    check 'Dropped: `a/b`, `file.md`, `--flag`, `-x`, `key:value`, `call()`, `/loa`, `two words`, `>>`, `*_TEST_MODE=1`, `9lives`, `x=y`.' --report
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"kernel tokens kept: 0;"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-9 an allowlisted token resolves; an allowlist of 31 entries fails" {
+    check 'Call `parse_it`.' --report
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"allowlisted parse_it"* ]]
+    : > "$W/a.txt"
+    for i in $(seq 1 31); do printf 'tok%02d  # reason\n' "$i" >> "$W/a.txt"; done
+    check 'Call `tok01`.'
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"has 31 entries, over the limit of 30"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-10 an allowlist of exactly 30 entries passes (stale entries only WARN)" {
+    : > "$W/a.txt"
+    for i in $(seq 1 30); do printf 'tok%02d  # reason\n' "$i" >> "$W/a.txt"; done
+    check 'Call `tok01`.'
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"allowlist entries: 30/30"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-11 a stale allowlist entry WARNs and still exits 0; a redundant one WARNs too" {
+    printf 'parse_it  # used\ngone_fn   # no longer in the kernel\nwidget    # the glossary defines it\n' > "$W/a.txt"
+    check 'Call `parse_it` on a `Widget`.'
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: allowlist entry 'gone_fn'"*"no longer occurs"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: allowlist entry 'widget'"*"already resolved by the glossary entry **Widget**"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-12 --json carries the report fields" {
+    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
+    printf 'parse_it  # used\ngone_fn   # stale\n' > "$W/a.txt"
+    check 'A `Widget`, `running`, `parse_it` and a `Sprocket`.' --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    echo "$output" | jq -e '
+        .ok == false and .kept == 4
+        and .counts == {defined: 1, alias: 1, allowlisted: 1, missing: 1}
+        and .missing == ["Sprocket"] and .stale_allowlist == ["gone_fn"]
+        and .allowlist_entries == 2 and .allowlist_max == 30
+        and (.tokens | map(.resolution)) == ["defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS"]
+        and (.tokens[0] | .token == "Widget" and .line == 1 and .entry == "Widget")
+        and (.tokens[3].entry == null)
+        and (.violations | length) == 1 and (.warnings | length) == 1' >/dev/null
+}
+

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/glossary-terms.bats
+#
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.2, §5.3) keeps every
+# backticked span of the kernel that matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$ outside
+# fenced code and fails unless each one resolves to a glossary **Term**, an
+# _Aliases_: token (case-insensitive, plural s/es folded) or an allowlist line
+# (at most 30). Every case below works on temp copies; the live kernel,
+# glossary and allowlist are only ever read.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh"
+    KERNEL="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+    GLOSSARY="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+    ALLOW="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
+    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/glossary"
+    W="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    printf '# Glossary: t\nTest vocabulary.\n\n## Language\n\n**Widget**: A thing.\n\n**Run mode**: Unattended runs.\n_Aliases_: RUNNING, JACKED_OUT\n\n**Box**: A container.\n' > "$W/g.md"
+    printf '# test allowlist\nparse_it   # code identifier\n' > "$W/a.txt"
+}
+
+# check <kernel text>: run the checker on a temp kernel with the temp glossary and allowlist
+check() {
+    printf '%s\n' "$1" > "$W/k.md"
+    shift
+    run "$CHECK" --kernel "$W/k.md" --glossary "$W/g.md" --allowlist "$W/a.txt" "$@"
+}
+
+@test "GT-1 the live kernel, framework glossary and allowlist pass" {
+    run "$CHECK"
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"missing: 0"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"PASS"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-2 removing a term from a copy of the glossary fails and names the token" {
+    grep -v '^_Aliases_: br$' "$GLOSSARY" > "$W/glossary.md"
+    run "$CHECK" --glossary "$W/glossary.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `br`'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"define **br**"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"_Aliases_: line"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"allowlist it in"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-3 removing the run mode entry from a copy fails on each of its aliases" {
+    awk '/^\*\*Run mode\*\*:/ { skip = 1; next } skip && /^_Aliases_:/ { skip = 0; next } { skip = 0; print }' "$GLOSSARY" > "$W/glossary.md"
+    run "$CHECK" --glossary "$W/glossary.md"
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `RUNNING`'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `HALTED`'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `JACKED_OUT`'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-4 matching is case-insensitive and folds s and es plurals" {
+    check 'Use a `widget`, two `Widgets`, `boxes` and `BOX`.' --report
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     widget"*"-> Widget"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     Widgets"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     boxes"*"-> Box"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     BOX"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-4b a singular token resolves to a plural term" {
+    printf '# Glossary: t\nctx\n\n## Language\n\n**Beads**: A tracker.\n\n**Matches**: Pairs.\n' > "$W/g.md"
+    check 'One `bead`, one `match`, many `BEADS`.' --report
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     bead "*"-> Beads"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     match "*"-> Matches"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-5 an _Aliases_: token resolves to its entry; a multi-word term matches with - or _" {
+    check 'States: `running`, `JACKED_OUT`; also `run-mode` and `run_mode`.' --report
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"alias       running"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"alias       JACKED_OUT"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     run-mode"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"defined     run_mode"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-6 an undefined token fails; a token close to a term does not resolve by accident" {
+    check 'A `Widgetry` and a `Sprocket`.'
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `Widgetry`'* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `Sprocket`'* ]]

+    [[ "$output" == *"kernel tokens kept: 1;"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-8 the shape heuristic drops paths, files, flags, keys, calls, commands, phrases and operators" {
+    check 'Dropped: `a/b`, `file.md`, `--flag`, `-x`, `key:value`, `call()`, `/loa`, `two words`, `>>`, `*_TEST_MODE=1`, `9lives`, `x=y`.' --report
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"kernel tokens kept: 0;"* ]]
+}
+

+    check 'Call `parse_it`.' --report
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"allowlisted parse_it"* ]]
+    : > "$W/a.txt"

+

+    : > "$W/a.txt"
+    for i in $(seq 1 30); do printf 'tok%02d  # reason\n' "$i" >> "$W/a.txt"; done

+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

+}
+
+@test "GT-11 a stale allowlist entry WARNs and still exits 0; a redundant one WARNs too" {
+    printf 'parse_it  # used\ngone_fn   # no longer in the kernel\nwidget    # the glossary defines it\n' > "$W/a.txt"
+    check 'Call `parse_it` on a `Widget`.'

+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: allowlist entry 'widget'"*"already resolved by the glossary entry **Widget**"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GT-12 --json carries the report fields" {
+    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
+    printf 'parse_it  # used\ngone_fn   # stale\n' > "$W/a.txt"
+    check 'A `Widget`, `running`, `parse_it` and a `Sprocket`.' --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    echo "$output" | jq -e '
+        .ok == false and .kept == 4
+        and .counts == {defined: 1, alias: 1, allowlisted: 1, missing: 1}
+        and .missing == ["Sprocket"] and .stale_allowlist == ["gone_fn"]
+        and .allowlist_entries == 2 and .allowlist_max == 30
+        and (.tokens | map(.resolution)) == ["defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS"]
+        and (.tokens[0] | .token == "Widget" and .line == 1 and .entry == "Widget")
+        and (.tokens[3].entry == null)
+        and (.violations | length) == 1 and (.warnings | length) == 1' >/dev/null
+}

  step "Updating .gitignore for submodule mode..."

  local symlink_entries=(

    ".claude/checksums.json"

    ".claude/aleph"
    ".claude/commands/loa-aleph.md"
    ".claude/skills/loa-aleph"
  )

  # State and backup entries (not symlinks but must be gitignored)
  local state_entries=(
    ".loa-state/"
---MANIFEST-CTX---
    ".claude/defaults:../${submodule}/.claude/defaults"
  )

  # #842: items COPIED into the consumer tree instead of symlinked.
  # Required for files/dirs that Claude Code (or other subprocess-spawned
  # executors) reads/exec'd at runtime, where relative-symlink resolution
  # through `..` traversal fails on macOS. Tradeoff: after `git submodule
  # update --remote`, operators must re-run `mount-submodule.sh --force`
  # to pick up changes in these paths. The cost is small (~20 files) and
  # explicit (mount has to run on every submodule bump anyway).
  MANIFEST_COPY_DIRS=(
    ".claude/hooks:${submodule}/.claude/hooks"
  )

  MANIFEST_COPY_FILES=(
    ".claude/settings.json:${submodule}/.claude/settings.json"
  )

  # Phase 2: File and nested symlinks (deeper paths with 2-level relative targets)
  MANIFEST_FILE_SYMLINKS=(
    ".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md:../../${submodule}/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    ".claude/loa/reference:../../${submodule}/.claude/loa/reference"
    ".claude/loa/learnings:../../${submodule}/.claude/loa/learnings"
    ".claude/loa/feedback-ontology.yaml:../../${submodule}/.claude/loa/feedback-ontology.yaml"
    ".claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md:../../${submodule}/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
    ".claude/checksums.json:../${submodule}/.claude/checksums.json"
  )

  # Phase 3: Per-skill symlinks (dynamic — discovered from submodule content)
  MANIFEST_SKILL_SYMLINKS=()
  if [[ -d "${repo_root}/${submodule}/.claude/skills" ]]; then
    for skill_dir in "${repo_root}/${submodule}"/.claude/skills/*/; do
      if [[ -d "$skill_dir" ]]; then
        local skill_name
        skill_name=$(basename "$skill_dir")
        # cycle-115: receipt-managed by the pinned Aleph installer. This must be
        # a real directory in the consumer tree, never a submodule symlink.
        [[ "$skill_name" == "loa-aleph" ]] && continue
        MANIFEST_SKILL_SYMLINKS+=(".claude/skills/${skill_name}:../../${submodule}/.claude/skills/${skill_name}")
      fi
    done
  fi

  # Phase 4: Per-command symlinks (dynamic — discovered from submodule content)
  MANIFEST_CMD_SYMLINKS=()
  if [[ -d "${repo_root}/${submodule}/.claude/commands" ]]; then

        MANIFEST_CMD_SYMLINKS+=(".claude/commands/${cmd_name}:../../${submodule}/.claude/commands/${cmd_name}")
      fi
    done

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: a new `red-test-check.sh`, a `--type glossary` validator plus a date-gated `### Seams Under Test` rule in `validate-artifact.sh`, `tools/check-glossary-terms.sh` with a CI workflow, two glossaries, an allowlist, fixtures, four bats suites and prose edits to six skill files; three mount lists gain `.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md`.

What is good: the code was verified, not just read. In a scratch tree with the PR applied (mawk 1.3.4, bash 5.2, git worktrees), all four new suites pass — `glossary-terms` 20/20, `glossary-validator` 19/19, `sprint-seams` 10/10 (SEAMS-8 skips by design outside the cycle-128 checkout), `red-test-check` 17/17. `tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --report` passes on the live kernel (16 tokens kept, 0 missing), both glossaries validate clean, the cycle-127 fixture gains only the WARN the test expects, the pinned `actions/checkout` SHA is genuinely v4.3.1, the three mount/gitignore lists are consistent, argv-injection guards on `--red/--green/--test-file` work (RTC-12), and the honest-scope header of `red-test-check.sh` is a model of saying what a check does not prove.

For the two most common layouts those directories carry absolute back-references into the live tree (a Python editable install's `.pth`, npm/pnpm workspace links), so the "red" and "green" runs both execute the live working copy, not `RED_SHA`/`GREEN_SHA`. The fix is small (opt-in linking, or refuse to link a directory with back-references, or verify the resolved module path lies inside the worktree).

Five MEDIUM and ten LOW observations follow, including three demonstrated by running the code (noexec `TMPDIR` → false `NOT_A_RED`; "e.g." counted as a sentence; a non-ISO header date silently downgrades the seams rule to WARN). - **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222-227` — `link_deps` symlinks the live tree's dependency directories (`DEP_DIRS`, line 47) into the red and green worktrees by default; when such a directory carries an absolute back-reference to the live tree, both runs test the live working copy instead of the two commits, and the verdict is wrong.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222-227` (also `:47`, `:346`)
**Issue:** A Python editable install (`pip install -e .`, PEP 660) writes a `.pth`/finder into `.venv/.../site-packages` that resolves `import pkg` to the live tree's absolute `src/` path; npm/pnpm/yarn workspaces place `node_modules/@scope/pkg -> ../../packages/pkg` links that resolve relative to the live `node_modules`. Linked into a worktree, `.venv/bin/python` (or `node`) in the red worktree imports the live tree's code. Reproduced in this review with a real venv and an `__editable__.pkg.pth` pointing at `<repo>/src`, red commit = failing test + buggy `add`, green = fixed `add`, live tree = green:
```
$ red-test-check.sh --red $RED -- .venv/bin/python tests/test_add.py
red-test-check: the test passes at the red commit: it does not reproduce the bug
red-test-check: red f37f831c exit 0; green 48fa83d4 exit 0; linked deps: .venv
pkg imported from /home/evaluser/rr/fx2/src/pkg/__init__.py
verdict: DECOY            (exit 3)
$ red-test-check.sh --red $RED --no-link-deps -- .venv/bin/python tests/test_add.py
red-test-check: the red run exited 127 (command not found or not executable)
verdict: NOT_A_RED        (exit 4)
```
**Why This Matters:** The script's purpose (header lines 3-18) is to prove "red fails by assertion and green passes"; here a correct red-before-green is reported as a decoy, and a live tree that differs from either commit yields arbitrary `VERIFIED`/`DECOY` mixes (a fix commit that also edits the test can read `VERIFIED` while the source change was never exercised). `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:219` instructs the reviewer to run this and "cite its output for 'Test fails with current code'", and `head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43` makes exit 0 an acceptance criterion, so the error propagates into gate decisions. The header (lines 27-30) warns only that writes land in the live copy, not that the code under test can be the live tree. Neither default has a working path for the standard Python `src/` layout.
**Required Fix:** Make linking opt-in (`--link-deps`) with `--setup` as the documented way to install into the worktree, or keep the default but refuse to link a directory that carries back-references (any `*.pth`/`__editable__*` under a linked `site-packages`; any symlink inside `node_modules` whose target lies outside it; any `vendor`/`target` that is itself a symlink), with a clear message naming the directory; alternatively, after linking, resolve the package under test (`python -c 'import pkg; print(pkg.__file__)'`-style probe, or `node -p "require.resolve(...)"`) and fail closed with a distinct verdict when the path is outside the worktree. Add RTC cases for an editable `.pth` and a workspace symlink proving the refusal, and state the limitation in the header and in `micro-sprint.md:43`.
**Reference:** CWE-706 (use of incorrectly-resolved name or reference); SDD D-7.5..D-7.7 as cited by the script header (the SDD itself is not in this workspace).

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-20
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (= pr/PR.md)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: a new `red-test-check.sh`, a `--type glossary` validator plus a date-gated `### Seams Under Test` rule in `validate-artifact.sh`, `tools/check-glossary-terms.sh` with a CI workflow, two glossaries, an allowlist, fixtures, four bats suites and prose edits to six skill files; three mount lists gain `.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md`.

What is good: the code was verified, not just read. In a scratch tree with the PR applied (mawk 1.3.4, bash 5.2, git worktrees), all four new suites pass — `glossary-terms` 20/20, `glossary-validator` 19/19, `sprint-seams` 10/10 (SEAMS-8 skips by design outside the cycle-128 checkout), `red-test-check` 17/17. `tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --report` passes on the live kernel (16 tokens kept, 0 missing), both glossaries validate clean, the cycle-127 fixture gains only the WARN the test expects, the pinned `actions/checkout` SHA is genuinely v4.3.1, the three mount/gitignore lists are consistent, argv-injection guards on `--red/--green/--test-file` work (RTC-12), and the honest-scope header of `red-test-check.sh` is a model of saying what a check does not prove.

What blocks: one HIGH, reproduced. `red-test-check.sh` symlinks the live tree's `node_modules`/`.venv`/`vendor`/`target`/`.tox` into both worktrees by default. For the two most common layouts those directories carry absolute back-references into the live tree (a Python editable install's `.pth`, npm/pnpm workspace links), so the "red" and "green" runs both execute the live working copy, not `RED_SHA`/`GREEN_SHA`. Reproduced here with a real venv: a correct failing-test-then-fix pair reports `DECOY` (exit 3) and prints `pkg imported from <live tree>/src/pkg/__init__.py`; with `--no-link-deps` the interpreter is absent and it reports `NOT_A_RED` (exit 127). The reviewing skill tells the reviewer to cite this output as proof of "Test fails with current code", so the gate can certify a red-before-green that never ran. The fix is small (opt-in linking, or refuse to link a directory with back-references, or verify the resolved module path lies inside the worktree).

Five MEDIUM and ten LOW observations follow, including three demonstrated by running the code (noexec `TMPDIR` → false `NOT_A_RED`; "e.g." counted as a sentence; a non-ISO header date silently downgrades the seams rule to WARN). The cross-model dissent produced 7 findings (3 marked BLOCKING); triage below adopts one as the HIGH above, downgrades three to MEDIUM with reasons, folds two, and refutes one half with evidence.

`reviewer.md` carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough; per `pr/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md` there is no implementation report in this frozen evaluation and that pre-flight is skipped rather than applied as an automatic fail. The verdict rests on the HIGH.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality / correctness of the red-before-green gate

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222-227` — `link_deps` symlinks the live tree's dependency directories (`DEP_DIRS`, line 47) into the red and green worktrees by default; when such a directory carries an absolute back-reference to the live tree, both runs test the live working copy instead of the two commits, and the verdict is wrong.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222-227` (also `:47`, `:346`)
**Issue:** A Python editable install (`pip install -e .`, PEP 660) writes a `.pth`/finder into `.venv/.../site-packages` that resolves `import pkg` to the live tree's absolute `src/` path; npm/pnpm/yarn workspaces place `node_modules/@scope/pkg -> ../../packages/pkg` links that resolve relative to the live `node_modules`. Linked into a worktree, `.venv/bin/python` (or `node`) in the red worktree imports the live tree's code. Reproduced in this review with a real venv and an `__editable__.pkg.pth` pointing at `<repo>/src`, red commit = failing test + buggy `add`, green = fixed `add`, live tree = green:
```
$ red-test-check.sh --red $RED -- .venv/bin/python tests/test_add.py
red-test-check: the test passes at the red commit: it does not reproduce the bug
red-test-check: red f37f831c exit 0; green 48fa83d4 exit 0; linked deps: .venv
pkg imported from /home/evaluser/rr/fx2/src/pkg/__init__.py
verdict: DECOY            (exit 3)
$ red-test-check.sh --red $RED --no-link-deps -- .venv/bin/python tests/test_add.py
red-test-check: the red run exited 127 (command not found or not executable)
verdict: NOT_A_RED        (exit 4)
```
**Why This Matters:** The script's purpose (header lines 3-18) is to prove "red fails by assertion and green passes"; here a correct red-before-green is reported as a decoy, and a live tree that differs from either commit yields arbitrary `VERIFIED`/`DECOY` mixes (a fix commit that also edits the test can read `VERIFIED` while the source change was never exercised). `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:219` instructs the reviewer to run this and "cite its output for 'Test fails with current code'", and `head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43` makes exit 0 an acceptance criterion, so the error propagates into gate decisions. The header (lines 27-30) warns only that writes land in the live copy, not that the code under test can be the live tree. Neither default has a working path for the standard Python `src/` layout.
**Required Fix:** Make linking opt-in (`--link-deps`) with `--setup` as the documented way to install into the worktree, or keep the default but refuse to link a directory that carries back-references (any `*.pth`/`__editable__*` under a linked `site-packages`; any symlink inside `node_modules` whose target lies outside it; any `vendor`/`target` that is itself a symlink), with a clear message naming the directory; alternatively, after linking, resolve the package under test (`python -c 'import pkg; print(pkg.__file__)'`-style probe, or `node -p "require.resolve(...)"`) and fail closed with a distinct verdict when the path is outside the worktree. Add RTC cases for an editable `.pth` and a workspace symlink proving the refusal, and state the limitation in the header and in `micro-sprint.md:43`.
**Reference:** CWE-706 (use of incorrectly-resolved name or reference); SDD D-7.5..D-7.7 as cited by the script header (the SDD itself is not in this workspace).

---

## Observations

Non-blocking. Severities are the damage if the scenario happens; confidence is how sure I am that it does.

### 1. red-test-check.sh robustness

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:183` — the worktrees live under `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/..."`; on a host whose temp filesystem is mounted `noexec` (this sandbox's `/tmp` is), a test command that is a script inside the tree (`-- ./run-tests.sh`, `-- scripts/test`) exits 126 at both commits and the gate reports `NOT_A_RED` for a legitimate red.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:183` (classification at `:326`)
**Suggestion:** Create the scratch directory under the repository (`$MAIN/.git/red-test-check.XXXXXX` or `$MAIN/.run/`) with `TMPDIR` as the fallback, or honour a dedicated override; when a run exits 126 and the tail contains `Permission denied`, name the probable cause in the message. Reproduced: `TMPDIR=/tmp red-test-check.sh --red $RED -- ./run-tests.sh` → `timeout: failed to run command './run-tests.sh': Permission denied`, `verdict: NOT_A_RED`, exit 4; the same pair with an exec-capable `TMPDIR` → `VERIFIED`.
**Benefit:** No false blocks on hardened CI runners and containers.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43` — the new acceptance criterion reads "does not weaken the test (`red-test-check.sh … ` exits 0)", but a green commit that only rewrites the test to pass is a stderr `WARN` with exit 0 (`head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:180`; RTC-14 at `head/tests/unit/red-test-check.bats:238` asserts exactly this), and `--json` (`:135-145`) carries no `warnings` field at all, so a machine consumer never sees it.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43`, `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:180`, `:135`
**Suggestion:** Either give the test-only case its own verdict and exit code (e.g. `TEST_ONLY`, exit 6) so the AC "exits 0" means what it says, or add `warnings: [...]` to the JSON object and reword the AC to "exits 0 and the reviewer confirms the red test is unchanged at green". The path-based check is also defeated by a fix commit that touches any non-test file (a comment), which the header should say.
**Benefit:** The AC stops over-claiming; `--json` consumers (run mode, graders) get the signal.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:52-70` — `NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS` covers pytest collection/import errors (`:61-62`) but not pytest setup errors (`ERROR at setup`, `fixture 'x' not found`), unittest's loader (`Failed to import test module`), or jest's `Test suite failed to run`; a red whose test never reached its assertion because a fixture was missing reads as an assertion failure, and a green that adds the fixture reads `VERIFIED`. (Dissent DISS-001; downgraded from BLOCKING: the header states the honest scope and the reviewer still reads the test, and the listed runners' most common classes are covered.)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:52-70`
**Suggestion:** Add the three patterns above (one entry per runner, as the comment at `:49-50` asks) with RTC cases, and prefer structured results where cheap (pytest `--junitxml`/`-rA` summary line, `go test -json`) so "error" and "fail" are told apart by the runner, not by grep.
**Benefit:** Fewer false reds accepted as reproduction.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:270-277` and `:198-205` — on the no-`timeout` path the watcher's `TERM → sleep 2 → KILL` escalation (`:256-262`) is cancelled: `wait "$RUN_PID"` returns as soon as the direct child dies from the TERM and the script immediately `kill`s the watcher (`:275`) before its KILL reaches the group, so a grandchild that ignores TERM survives (the header at `:33-34` promises "TERM, then KILL after 2 s"). On every path, `cleanup` (`:198-205`) sends one TERM and proceeds straight to `worktree remove --force` and `rm -rf` without waiting or escalating. (Dissent DISS-002 and DISS-C-004 folded; downgraded: requires a TERM-ignoring descendant and, for the first, a host without `timeout`/`gtimeout` — e.g. stock macOS.)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:270-277`, `:198-205`
**Suggestion:** In `run_bounded`, when `$flag` exists let the watcher finish (wait for it) before clearing; in `cleanup`, after TERM poll `kill -0` for ≤2 s, then `kill -KILL -- -$RUN_PID`, `wait` it, and run `worktree prune` again after `rm -rf "$SCRATCH"` so a failed `remove` is still pruned.
**Benefit:** No orphaned processes writing into removed directories or into linked live-tree dependency directories.

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:216` — `git worktree add --detach` does not initialise submodules; in a consumer project mounted in submodule mode the worktree's `.loa/` is empty and every manifest symlink under `.claude/` dangles, so a test that sources a framework script fails identically at red and green (`GREEN_FAILS`, exit 1) with no hint of the cause and no `NOT_A_RED` pattern matching "No such file or directory". **Suggestion:** After `worktree add`, `git -C "$path" submodule update --init --recursive` when `.gitmodules` exists, or link the live `.loa` the way dependencies are linked; add the `.claude/…: No such file or directory` shape to the heuristics.
